citation.title: Distributed design optimization of multi-component systems using meta models and topology optimization
citation.authors: Lukas Krischer, Felix Endress, Tobias Wanninger, Markus Zimmermann

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: The proposed Informed Decomposition produced designs up to 12.9% heavier than monolithic optimization in the reported examples.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No speed-up factor is stated; the article says computational time was not explicitly investigated.
claim.alternatives: Conclusion says each subproblem is smaller and computation time may be significantly reduced, but this is qualitative.

baseline.implementation: MATLAB; article states results can be replicated with MATLAB
baseline.problem_size: P1: 2 components, each 20 x 8 x 8 elements; P2: 4-component robot
baseline.data_generation_cost: sample generation for offline database described as computationally expensive, not quantified (Discussion)
baseline.quality_metric: system mass and displacement / stiffness constraints
baseline.quality_gap: up to 12.9% heavier than monolithic optimization (Abstract)

R1.evidence: Primary outcome is a design-mass quality comparison, not a measured speed comparison (Abstract).

R2.evidence: Methods and Discussion do not establish a listed R2 baseline weakness.

R3.evidence: Discussion states offline sample generation is computationally expensive and notes training is not included in the potential time reduction, but gives no cost accounting or break-even number.

R4.evidence: Sections 5–7 assess physical feasibility and system stiffness against requirements; the paper says all outcomes met requirements but does not report a count/rate of failed or infeasible designs.

reporting.n_test_cases: 2 design problems: P1 and P2; P1 includes 6 load cases and P2 includes 100 (Abstract, Sections 5–6)

notes: The article explicitly states that computational time was not investigated; its reduction is a prospective claim. Published full text says results are reproducible using MATLAB and the derivations, but no public code is identified.
